entries.title: Multi-course admin navigation
entries.content:

An example admin system showed course-aware navigation and reporting. Dashboard and timesheet pages can expose separate course labels, course-specific summary and four-week views, and combined views. Course names are club configuration values and should not be treated as product knowledge, but the multi-course pattern is reusable.

entries.content:
Admin access exposes configuration categories and product warnings that are hidden or blocked from read-only roles.
Admin-visible System Configuration can include feature switches and club setup categories such as course-name configuration for multi-course installations and green-fee printer module settings. Specific enabled settings, club values, and warning state are instance-specific; support guidance should explain what the setting area controls and when staff should contact support for restricted or platform-level changes.

entries.content:

Support guidance should focus on how rate definitions connect to tee sheet bookings, online booking, reporting, and membership eligibility rather than recording exact rates.

entries.title: Reservation type online booking control
entries.content:
Reservation Types can control classification, display, and whether partially booked tee times remain available to online booking channels.
Admin help text showed an Allow Online Bookings control on reservation types. This setting determines whether partially booked tee times using that reservation type can continue to accept online bookings through connected online booking channels. Reservation types also affect timesheet display, filtering, reports, and booking workflows. Exact custom types and colours are club-specific; reusable guidance should explain the control and downstream effect.

entries.title: Configured Facilities workflow
entries.content:
Facilities can manage configured non-tee-sheet resources using booking, repeat, and resource controls.
A configured Facilities module exposes bookable resources with fields for reservation name, guests, room or facility, start and end times, repeat days, and repeat weeks. Product help indicates that adding a new reservation requires all selected time slots to be free, modifying a reservation overwrites only fields entered by the user, cancelling clears reservation values, and cut/copy/paste tools can move or duplicate reservations. Resource names and actual bookings are club-specific and should be excluded from template knowledge.

Member competition setup controls booking eligibility, charging, guest charging, waiting lists, and refund behavior.

entries.title: Open competition course setup
entries.content:
Open competition setup defines course, dates, times, booking format, playing format, fees, mixed team rules, and online booking go-live controls.
Admin access showed Open Competition fields including course, competition date, start and end time, competition name, booking format, playing format, competition type, number of holes, member and visitor green fees, mixed member/visitor team permission, and booking available date/time. Product help indicates that reservation name matching links configured competitions to tee times, that booking and playing formats affect the booking structure, and that the go-live date/time controls online availability. entries.title: Staff [redacted-name] access profile
entries.content:
A Staff [redacted-name] account can sign into the BRS admin area and view operational pages without being able to access many configuration pages.
Staff [redacted-name] users can view dashboard, timesheet, search, reports, users summary, contacts, facilities, messages, and tools index pages. Configuration pages such as system configuration details, green fee setup, competition setup, timesheet message setup, and text messaging can return a privilege warning. This access level is suitable for gathering template knowledge from visible product structure while reducing the chance of changing club setup.

These links are the main orientation points for staff users moving between tee sheet operations, communication, facilities, contact records, user management, reporting, setup, and support content.

entries.content:
The dashboard gives staff an operational overview and shortcuts into key BRS areas.
The dashboard contains tee sheet utilisation widgets with date-range controls such as today, tomorrow, and custom ranges. It summarizes bookings and golfers and separates member and visitor activity. Dashboard shortcut groups include course status, green fees, messaging, online booking links, competition links, tee time availability, golf event booking, online tee times menu, clubhouse PC login, and product/help links. These figures are club-state data and should not be used as product knowledge, but the widget structure and shortcut purposes are reusable.

The day timesheet has date navigation and alternate views including Timesheet, Summary, 4 Week, Month, and Year. Booking option controls allow staff to filter or prepare booking data by tee time, holes, reservation name, reservation type, players, buggies, repeat weeks, and green fee fields. The day view can include sunrise, sunset, and other timing markers and provides a print daily booking sheet link. Observed row contents, names, prices, and booking counts are club state and should not be ingested literally.

entries.title: Create a member profile workflow relationship map
entries.content:
Use the Memberships module, not Users, when the club is adding a normal member/customer membership profile. The observed Members list exposes the Members tab, FLEX MEMBERS, CREATE MEMBER, Search, Filter Active Members, Membership Type, Filter Columns, Download CSV Members, Print Members, and columns for Title, Email, Membership Card Number, Membership Type, Membership Status, and Actions.
Workflow: Create a member profile
Workflow family: Membership member profile management
Aliases: add a member; create a member; new member; add member in the system; member profile; membership profile; create member profile; membership member
Route 1: Create a normal membership profile
Route 1 actor: BRS admin or club staff with Memberships access
Route 1 preconditions: The request is about creating a club member or membership profile.; Do not use this route for staff, admin, receptionist, pro shop, password, permission, or login-account questions.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships from the main navigation menu.
Route 1 step 2: Open Members in the Memberships navigation.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBER on the Members screen.
Route 1 step 4: Complete the required fields on the create-member screen, then set the membership type/status and any club-specific membership details shown there.
Route 1 step 5: Save/create the member only after checking the details entered for the member.
Route 1 step 6: Return to Memberships > Members and use Search, Filter Active Members, Membership Type, or the Actions column to confirm the new member profile appears.
Route 1 outcome: A membership profile exists in the Memberships member list.
Route 1 verification: The member appears on Memberships > Members.; The visible list columns can be checked: Title, Email, Membership Card Number, Membership Type, Membership Status, and Actions.
Related workflow 1: Membership type setup
Related workflow 1 type: prerequisite-or-context
Related workflow 1 reason: A member profile may need a Membership Type before it can be created or correctly categorized.
Related workflow 1 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about the type/category/status/flex setup needed for the new member.
Related workflow 1 include when: membership type; member type; category; status; flex; flexi; flexible
Related workflow 2: Membership subscription setup
Related workflow 2 type: billing-setup-context
Related workflow 2 reason: Default subscriptions and subscription application can affect the member after the profile exists.
Related workflow 2 answer use: Pull this in when the user asks about subscriptions, subs, charges, fees, default subscriptions, or what the member should be billed for.
Related workflow 2 include when: subscription; subscriptions; subs; charge; fee; default
Related workflow 3: Membership billing and payments
Related workflow 3 type: post-create-workflow
Related workflow 3 reason: Creating a member and billing that member are separate workflows that often happen together.
Related workflow 3 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks how to bill, invoice, take payment, create bills, check unpaid bills, or review balances for the new member.
Related workflow 3 include when: bill; billing; invoice; payment; owe; owed; balance; unpaid
Related workflow 4: Flexible membership account management
Related workflow 4 type: conditional-related-workflow
Related workflow 4 reason: Flexible membership profiles depend on flexible membership type setup and flexi wallet/account handling.
Related workflow 4 answer use: Pull this in when the question mentions flex, flexi, flexible, wallet, points, balance, or account balance.
Related workflow 4 include when: flex; flexi; flexible; wallet; points; balance
Related workflow 5: Member messaging
Related workflow 5 type: follow-up-workflow
Related workflow 5 reason: After creating or selecting members, staff may need to email or text selected members, membership types, or member groups.
Related workflow 5 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about notifying, emailing, texting, messaging, or selecting members.
Related workflow 5 include when: email; mail; text; sms; message; notify
Related workflow 6: Bulk member and contact upload
Related workflow 6 type: alternative-route
Related workflow 6 reason: Bulk upload/import is a different route from creating a single member manually.
Related workflow 6 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about importing, uploading, CSV, spreadsheet, many members, or bulk member creation.
Related workflow 6 include when: upload; import; csv; spreadsheet; bulk; many members; multiple members
Related workflow 7: User account and login management
Related workflow 7 type: confusable-but-separate
Related workflow 7 reason: Users > Add New creates or manages BRS user/login accounts and is not the normal route for adding a membership profile.
Related workflow 7 answer use: Use only when the question explicitly says staff/admin/user/login/password/permissions or asks for a member login account.

Variant 2: Flexible wallets dashboard visibility

Variant 2 answer impact: Use Memberships > Settings > General and the Display Flexible Wallets table on dashboard checkbox.
Variant 3: Wallet/account setup
Variant 3 applies when: The user asks about configuring wallets, account units, auto assignment, active state, or minimum balance.
Variant 3 answer impact: Use Memberships > Accounts, not Membership Types.

Route 1 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE.

Route 1 step 7: Use Minimum Age and Maximum Age only if the type should be age-limited.

preconditions: User is signed into the BRS admin area.
The Contacts module is enabled for the club.
steps: Open "Contacts" from the main navigation menu.
Click "Add New" on the Contacts page.
Complete "CompanyName" and choose "Other" in "Category".
Tick "Disabled" when creating a temporary or inactive contact.
Use the contact detail fields such as "Title1", "Firstname1", "Surname1", "Email1", telephone fields, address fields, and "CustomerNotes" as needed.
Leave marketing consent boxes such as "Email", "Text Message", "Post", and "Phone" unticked unless the contact has consented.
Click "Add" to create the contact.
Use contact search/view to confirm the contact appears.
Open the contact record and click "Delete" to remove the temporary contact.
Search again and confirm the temporary contact no longer appears.
routes.outcome: A temporary disabled contact can be created, found, deleted, and verified as removed.
verification: Temporary test contact appeared in Contacts search after creation.

Cleanup verification was completed in a follow-up cleanup run for marker "[temporary test contact]".

entries.title: Workflow family: Move a tee sheet booking
entries.content:
Use this family when the user wording is about moving, transferring, or rescheduling a tee sheet booking. Service wording such as buggy, trolley, caddie, or club hire is a variant unless observed evidence proves a separate service-specific route.
Workflow: Move a tee sheet booking
Workflow family: Move a tee sheet booking
Aliases: move a booking; reschedule a booking; transfer a booking; move a visitor booking; move a member booking; move a booking with services attached
Variant 1: Booking with attached service or hire item
Variant 1 applies when: The wording includes a buggy, trolley, caddie, club hire, or another service attached to the booking.
Variant 1 answer impact: Use the same move-booking route unless test-system evidence proves the service has a separate move workflow.
Variant 1 same workflow as: Move a tee sheet booking
Variant 2: Paid booking
Variant 2 applies when: The booking has BRS payment information attached.
Variant 2 answer impact: Use Cut from inside Booking Details so payment information remains attached, then check payment status after moving.
Route 1: Booking Details cut and paste route
Route 1 actor: Admin or staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The booking exists on the tee sheet.; The user can open Booking Details.
Route 1 step 1: Click the tee time to open the Booking Details page.
Route 1 step 2: Click Cut from inside the Booking Details page.
Route 1 step 3: Return to the tee sheet.
Route 1 step 4: Go to the new date if the booking is being moved to a different day.
Route 1 step 5: Tick the checkbox beside the target tee time.
Route 1 step 6: Click Paste.
Route 1 step 7: Check the payment status after moving the booking.
Route 1 outcome: The booking is moved while keeping payment information attached.
Route 1 verification: Check the moved booking on the target tee time.; Check payment status after the move.
Rollback policy: No write action is required to answer from this approved workflow. Future automatic write exploration must create only test records and verify rollback.
Exploration status: starter-approved-local-guidance

entries.title: BRS system ingestion principles
entries.content:
# BRS system ingestion principles

The BRS system crawler is used to learn reusable product behaviour, not to copy a club's private setup.

Approved knowledge includes menu structure, page purpose, setting names, product-authored help text, workflow steps, report names, filters, and relationships between areas such as tee sheet, payments, competitions, memberships, reports, and system configuration.

Do not store member names, visitor names, staff names, email addresses, phone numbers, booking references, payment amounts, green fee values, transaction identifiers, custom club policy text, or exact audit timestamps. When audit metadata is useful, record only that the product exposes last-modified information.

System knowledge must be treated as template knowledge unless it has been reviewed and approved as broadly applicable product guidance.
